transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the pre-publication check-in for 'Glass Harbor.' Before we finalize the catalog, I need to hear from submissions and technical screening staff on two things: first, the premiere status — our draft still has it marked 'for confirmation,' and we need to know whether it qualifies as a national premiere. Second, the runtime — the draft lists 94 minutes, which would exceed the 90-minute cap for national competition entries. If either issue can't be resolved in favor of national competition eligibility, we'll need to move the film to the panorama program. Does anyone have updates on the premiere status or the master file?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the national festival database yesterday and confirmed that 'Glass Harbor' already had a public screening at the Coastline Film Week in this country. I recorded the result in my local review notes, but the database export feeding Mara's catalog review has not refreshed, which is why the draft still shows premiere status as 'for confirmation.'
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed ingest quality control this morning and confirmed that the filmmaker's approved festival cut is an 88-minute DCP, not the 94-minute catalog draft. The QC report is waiting in the technical queue and has not yet been attached to the programming record.
transcript.speaker: A3

Refresh the database export so the premiere status reflects the confirmed Coastline Film Week screening.
